title: Maximal Range That Each Element Is Maximum In It
description:
You are given a 0-indexed array `nums` of **distinct** integers. For each index `i`, find the longest contiguous subarray that contains index `i` and in which `nums[i]` is the largest element.

Return an array `ans` of the same length where `ans[i]` is the length of that subarray. Since each element is trivially the maximum of the subarray consisting of itself, every `ans[i]` is at least `1`.

**Example 1:**
```
Input: nums = [2,8,1,6,3]
Output: [1,5,1,3,1]
Explanation: 2 is blocked by 8 on its right, so only [2]. 8 is the largest, so it covers all 5 elements. 6 is blocked by 8 on its left and reaches the end: [1,6,3] has length 3. 1 and 3 are alone.
```

**Example 2:**
```
Input: nums = [9,6,3]
Output: [3,2,1]
Explanation: The array is strictly decreasing, so each element extends right to the end but never left: ans[i] = n - i.
```

**Example 3:**
```
Input: nums = [7,3,9]
Output: [2,1,3]
Explanation: 7 extends right over 3 to give length 2, 3 is alone, and 9 covers the whole array.
```

examples.explanation: 2 is blocked by 8 on its right, so only [2]. 8 is the largest, so it covers all 5 elements. 6 is blocked by 8 on its left and reaches the end: [1,6,3] has length 3. 1 and 3 are alone.
The array is strictly decreasing, so each element extends right to the end but never left: ans[i] = n - i.
7 extends right over 3 to give length 2, 3 is alone, and 9 covers the whole array.

constraints: All values in nums are distinct
solution_approach: The brute force expands left and right from every index while neighbours are smaller, O(n^2) in the worst case (e.g. a sorted array). The optimal solution uses a monotonic decreasing stack to compute, for every index, its previous greater element L[i] and next greater element R[i] (with -1 and n as sentinels). nums[i] is the maximum of every subarray strictly between those two, so ans[i] = R[i] - L[i] - 1. A single pass that pops smaller elements when a larger one arrives fills both arrays. Time O(n), space O(n).
hints: The range for nums[i] stops exactly at the first larger element on each side.
So the problem reduces to finding the previous greater and the next greater element of every index.
Use a stack of indices with decreasing values: when nums[i] pops index j, set R[j] = i; after popping, the stack top (or -1) is L[i]. Then ans[i] = R[i] - L[i] - 1.
follow_up_questions: How would you handle duplicates if 'maximum' allowed ties?
Can you use the same ranges to compute the sum of maximums over all subarrays?
